sections.h2: Where does the Macomb County Register of Deeds operate?
sections.html:
The register works inside the county Clerk's office at 120 N. Main St. in Mount Clemens, MI 48043, staffed on weekdays until 4:15 p.m. after an 8 a.m. start. The phone is 586-469-7953 and the email is registerofdeeds@macombgov.org. An online booking tool lets you reserve a visit, and the same page links a land records search, a status page for documents already submitted, and a mail-in request for certified copies.

Macomb is a charter county on the eastern edge of Michigan. It touches Lake St. Clair, borders Detroit to the south, and had 881,217 residents in 2020, the third largest population in the state after Wayne and Oakland. Its 27 cities, townships and villages include Warren, Sterling Heights, St. Clair Shores, Roseville, Eastpointe, Fraser, Utica, Romeo and Armada, with the largest share of people living south of M-59 (Hall Road). I-94 and I-696 cut across the southern part, and Selfridge Air National Guard Base sits at Mount Clemens.

With that many parcels, return times stretch. The office's FAQ says to expect recorded documents back roughly 6 to 8 weeks after the recording date, so cite a correct RETURN TO name and address on page one.

sections.h2: What do deeds and searches cost in Macomb County?
sections.html:
Flat pricing applies: $30 for a deed, mortgage, lis pendens or certified court paper, whatever its page count. A document that releases several instruments adds $3 each after the first. The county says $4 of each fee goes to the state survey fund, with exceptions for fixture filings, liens, state deeds, plats and tax reversion papers.

Searches and copies are priced separately, and the schedule includes oddities such as large-format plats and Uniform Commercial Code filings. Plat copies run $3.50 at 11 by 17 inches and $4.50 at 18 by 24, with $2.50 postage if mailed. Fixture filings and UCC terminations are $30 each, the same as a deed. A UCC search is $12 per debtor name, made up of $6 for the name search and $3 each for state and federal tax lien certificates, and a copy of a UCC filing is $2 a page. Personal property financing statements filed after July 1, 2001 go to the state UCC office and do not show up in the register's searches, so the register's results cover fixture filings and similar land-based items.

sections.h2: Which Macomb County deeds need a treasurer's certificate?
sections.html:
Anything carrying a warranty clause. The register's fee page says warranty deeds, deeds with a covenant clause, land contracts and assignments of land contract need certification from the County Treasurer before recording. Since July 1, 2015 the certificate costs $5 for up to five legal descriptions and $0.20 for each extra description. The authority is MCL 211.135.

The Treasurer, at 586-469-5190, confirms that tax is paid up for the five years before the deed date. The Land File office at 586-469-5313 supplies legal descriptions, and the register's FAQ lists the same number plus the local assessor as free sources for a taxpayer's name and address. Questions on transfer tax go to 586-469-5309.

Quitclaim deeds without a warranty covenant skip the certificate. Macomb also posts its own quitclaim form on the register's page, along with a construction lien claim form and a sheriff's deed payoff request. The county says it supplies these forms without any warranty about their legal effect.

sections.h2: Is the register's first-page cover sheet really needed?
sections.html:
It is when page one fails the margin rule. The county's recording requirements say a first page needs a 2.5 inch top margin and a half inch on all other sides. If it falls short, attach a cover page that states the document's title. This matters for older deeds that crowd the top edge.

The county also stresses a few other points:

  • Names typed or stamped under original signatures must match the notary's acknowledgment.
  • A deed must show each grantee's address and the drafter's name and address.
  • Instruments signed before April 16, 2017 had to state the marital status of male grantors.
  • Court orders are recorded only if certified and sealed by the court clerk.
  • A death certificate cannot be attached to another document since September 18, 2018.

Statutory sources are in MCL 565.201, and the county offers a link to common document problems.

sections.h2: How do I change who is on a Macomb County deed?
sections.html:
To add a person, record a quit claim deed, typed or in black ink, signed and notarized. The cost is $30. The register advises hiring an attorney if the goal is to avoid probate. To drop a deceased owner, record a certified copy of the death certificate for $30. The survivorship wording on the deed decides whether probate is still needed.

A paid-off mortgage does not produce a new deed. The lender sends a discharge, release or satisfaction of mortgage for recording, and the deed you received at purchase stays your title. Lost your copy? A recorded copy is just as good as the original, and you can ask in person, by mail or through the online search.

After any ownership change, the new owner must report it to the local assessor within 45 days. MCL 211.27a treats most deed transfers as a trigger to reset taxable value, with carve-outs for spouses and for residential transfers among close family.

sections.h2: How does a payoff letter work after a Macomb County sheriff's sale?
sections.html:
Someone entitled to redeem after a sheriff's sale can ask the register for a payoff letter for $25, paid with the request form. It is ready after 2 business days, and the form can be mailed or dropped off. The state statute behind it is MCL 600.3240, which lets registers in counties of 750,000 to 1,500,000 people determine the amount using only recorded affidavits, and it frees the county of liability for an incorrect figure.

The redemption itself must be paid by certified or cashier's check by 4 p.m. on the last working day of the redemption period. A $5 care and custody fee applies, and it is already in a figure from the register. The office then issues a letter confirming that funds arrived, and the sheriff's deed holder prepares the redemption certificate for recording.

The register also offers a Fraud Notify alerts system. Owners who sign up are warned when a document is recorded under their names, a safeguard worth having when a house is vacant or being sold.

faqs.q: What is the recording charge at the Mount Clemens register of deeds?
faqs.a: It is $30 per document regardless of length. A warranty deed adds the $5 treasurer certificate for up to five legal descriptions, and extra descriptions are $0.20 each.

faqs.q: How soon do recorded Macomb County deeds come back?
faqs.a: Roughly 6 to 8 weeks from the recording date, according to the county's FAQ. A correct RETURN TO name and address on the document helps it reach the right person.

faqs.q: Where can I see whether a Macomb County document has been recorded?
faqs.a: Use the status of recorded documents page on the register's site, or call 586-469-7953. The land records search lets you request copies, and search and copy fees apply.

faqs.q: What does Macomb County charge in transfer tax?
faqs.a: The county rate is 55 cents per $500 under MCL 207.504, and the state adds $3.75 per $500. On a $310,000 sale, 620 units give $341 to the county and $2,325 to the state, or $2,666 combined. Call 586-469-5309 for details.

faqs.q: Can I mail a deed to the Macomb County register?
faqs.a: Yes. The county's FAQ says a completed quit claim deed can be mailed in or brought in for recording, and certified copy requests are accepted through the U.S. Mail.
